To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
wheat variety Sonalika was found to have low nitrous oxide emission and high yield due to high efficiency in photosynthate allocation towards the developing grains.
wheat varieties with higher stomatal frequency and smaller xylem vessels have the potential to reduce N2O emissions.
the N2O flux from the soil surface was significantly different among the three varieties of wheat grown in a uniform soil and climatic condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a strategy for reducing N2O emissions from wheat by using low N2O-emitting varieties of wheat.
the identification and characterization of physiological and anatomically based traits in wheat varieties that can be used as a basis for developing strategies to reduce N2O emissions.
the identification of plant physiological and anatomically related factors contributing to differences among wheat varieties in N2O fluxes and their association with grain yield.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the low N2O emission is a result of low stomatal frequency and low transpiration in Sonalika variety.
wheat varieties that are more efficient in the use of water and photosynthate for grain yield production would also emit less N2O gas.
the low N2O-emitting varieties are the varieties that have high stomatal frequency, low mean vessel size, and high transpiration rate in the flag leaf.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the low emitting wheat variety Sonalika is a better choice for reducing the N2O emission and also for increasing the grain yield.

wheat genotypes with high stomatal frequency, high rate of transpiration, and large xylem vessels are associated with high N2O emission, whereas wheat genotypes with low stomatal frequency, low rate of transpiration and small xylem vessels have lower N2O emission.
the wheat genotypes having high stomatal frequency and smaller xylem vessels are likely to emit more nitrous oxide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N2O emission can be minimized by using wheat varieties that possess higher stomatal frequency and smaller xylem vessel size.
N2O emission from wheat crop is strongly influenced by genetic factors, and therefore, it should be possible to reduce emissions through selection of appropriate varieties.
